thread_analysis.thread_summary: Hosiden Corporation (contacts Masaki Hori, Yusuke Nomura) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Masaya Iida) for Bluetooth SIG certification of a wristband-type wearable device (smartwatch) module, spanning August through November 2024. The thread is unusually deep on post-2024 registration system mechanics -- inter-layer ICS consistency checks, DN assignment quirks, and RF PHY test scoping -- alongside standard RF PHY test execution and registration finalization logistics.
all_questions_found: Can a DN-bearing registration be achieved when combining an existing Controller Subsystem QDID and Host Subsystem QDID that fails the inter-layer consistency check, and if not directly, what's the best alternative strategy? (see thread_0025_case_01)

Does a 'Details'/'Default' DN display after an unmodified-design-reuse registration indicate a problem, and is re-branding with only a Q30-prefixed QDID valid for Bluetooth certification? (see thread_0025_case_02)
Can the RF PHY test scope (and fee) be reduced to 1M-only when the registration inherits a full 1M+2M ICS from an unmodified-Design Include? (see thread_0025_case_03)
What RF/BT test equipment does the lab use, and would the customer's own Rohde & Schwarz tester give equivalent results? (see thread_0025_case_04)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Standard quote tiers for module-with-antenna vs. SoC-direct-mounted vs. no-Profile-Subsystem-reference scenarios, RF test sample shipping logistics (Japan vs. Taiwan lab, export classification documents for cross-border shipment, customs documentation), Compliance Folder document submission (module spec sheet/block diagram/outline drawing acceptable via Bluetooth IC datasheet excerpts or a photo with a ruler for scale, plus antenna datasheet with radiation gain pattern), test report revision-control procedure after a product name correction, and final Review Page confirmation -- consistent with administrative content already documented in other threads.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread provides the most detailed documentation in this batch of the post-July-2024 inter-layer ICS consistency check mechanism, including the 'whack-a-mole' Mandatory-test cascade risk and a sophisticated restructuring strategy (SoC-as-Core-Controller-with-RF-PHY-report) for preserving DN-bearing registration value when a direct fix isn't practical. Case_02's DN display behavior documentation and case_03's ICS-vs-confirmation-report distinction for RF PHY scope are both concrete, reusable technical nuances that extend the already-documented post-2024 system knowledge base.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0025_case_01 through thread_0025_case_04 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_01 carries the highest strategic risk, since committing to a direct ICS-edit fix without anticipating the cascading Mandatory-test expansion, or failing to consider the DN-preserving restructuring alternative, could significantly increase cost and undermine the module's value to downstream OEM customers.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant proactively ran trial Consistency Checks in his own Workspace before committing the customer to a registration path, and when a direct fix proved impractical, devised and proposed a structurally different alternative rather than leaving the customer with only the no-DN fallback option.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When an existing-QDID combination fails the post-2024 inter-layer consistency check, don't default to either a blind ICS edit (risking a Mandatory-test cascade) or the no-DN fallback path without first checking whether a structural alternative (e.g., registering the SoC alone as Core Controller with its own RF PHY report) can preserve DN-bearing registration value for both the immediate customer and their downstream OEM customers; and when explaining unmodified-Design-Include registrations, proactively clarify the difference between the inherited (uneditable) ICS declaration and any separately-scoped confirmation-report testing, since customers may incorrectly assume the entire test scope is fixed when in fact some elements remain adjustable to match real hardware capability.
